incidents.vector: Unspecified intrusion exposed a patient records database.
incidents.impact: Patient names, emails, passport/ID numbers, dates of birth, emergency contacts, and bank account details were stolen.

incidents.vector: Not detailed in reporting.
incidents.impact: FBI confirmed North Korean state responsibility for a hack resulting in an estimated $6.3 billion in losses.

incidents.victim: Multiple hospitals, banks, and a pet food company
incidents.vector: AI-generated deepfake voice and video used to impersonate executives and lawyers and authorize fraudulent payments.
incidents.impact: Three men charged, two arrested in Spain and one detained in the UK, after defrauding victims of a combined $129 million.

incidents.victim: Crypto investment scam victims across Europe
incidents.vector: Phone-based social engineering directing victims to fake broker and investment platforms.
incidents.impact: Four suspects arrested in Ukraine after a scheme that defrauded victims across Europe of an estimated €4.3 million.

incidents.vector: Unspecified compromise; some data drawn from older breaches.
incidents.impact: Personal data from 34 French sports federations, including swimming, handball, basketball, rugby, tennis, and football bodies, was leaked online.

incidents.vector: Not specified; internal systems were disrupted.
incidents.impact: The agency failed to publish scheduled weekly price data, with releases delayed through Nov. 13, and some previously published data was removed from its site.

incidents.victim: Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani and other European officials
incidents.vector: Cyberattack followed by doxing of personal and official information.
incidents.impact: Confidential information on the Italian foreign minister and several EU/national officials (Eurojust, Europol, German BKA, Italian Postal Police) was obtained and offered for sale.

incidents.vector: Extortion threat email; no confirmed breach.
incidents.impact: Transactions suspended and customer assets moved to offline storage as a precaution following an extortion threat against the South Korean exchange.

incidents.victim: Financial-sector organizations in Southeast Asia and globally
incidents.vector: Agentic AI offensive framework (ARTEX) used to scan systems, exploit SSRF and file-upload flaws, and deploy open-source remote access trojans.
incidents.impact: Compromise of financial organizations primarily in Southeast Asia, with a smaller number of large financial organizations globally also affected.

incidents.vector: Not specified.
incidents.impact: Reported loss of $133 million.

incidents.vector: Spyware.
incidents.impact: Surveillance of opposition figures.

incidents.vector: Not specified.
incidents.impact: A newly emerged ransomware group, WhiteArmor, claims theft of 10GB of driver records, staff accounts, and delivery receipts, demanding a $5 million ransom; Maersk has not confirmed the claim.

incidents.victim: Global financial system (via MEXC Global exchange)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — financial fraud, with sanctioned state-linked networks
incidents.vector: Anti-money-laundering control failures allowed the exchange to process illicit transactions.
incidents.impact: A FinCEN order cuts MEXC Global off from the U.S. financial system after it facilitated an estimated $16 billion in illicit transactions since 2021, including ransomware and scam payments.

incidents.victim: Supermarket chains, cold-storage facilities, and blood banks across Europe
incidents.attacker: Unknown — pro-Kremlin hacktivist groups have claimed credit (unconfirmed)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of internet-exposed refrigeration controllers (Danfoss, Copeland, Dixell) via default credentials or known weaknesses.
incidents.impact: Forced defrost cycles destroyed inventory at hundreds of stores across 10+ countries, caused some fires, and briefly affected a French blood bank; CISA and FBI issued a joint advisory.

incidents.vector: Ransomware encryption of internal systems.
incidents.impact: On-site computers, checkout machines, WiFi, digital media services, and the mobile app were taken offline across 66 branches serving 2.3 million residents.

incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — scam and fraud network
incidents.vector: Digital-asset investment and romance scams run from forced-labor scam compounds, with proceeds laundered through shell companies.
incidents.impact: Treasury sanctions target a Southeast Asia-based network that has generated billions of dollars in illicit proceeds from victims worldwide.

incidents.vector: Not specified.
incidents.impact: A threat actor claims theft of approximately 100,000 customers' data; the claim is not yet confirmed by the company.

incidents.victim: Executive Office of the President (White House network)
incidents.vector: Staff devices running consumer residential-proxy applications.
incidents.impact: White House network IP addresses were rented out via 28 separate proxy services and used publicly 236 times in a month, exposing a sensitive government network.

incidents.vector: Not specified.
incidents.impact: All user passwords for the MyTUM student/employee portal, including admin accounts, were stolen, forcing the portal offline and mandatory password resets.

incidents.vector: Not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Card owner information was stolen; the company enabled 3D Secure for all cardholders in response.

incidents.vector: Stolen backup credentials and rogue domain-admin accounts used to abuse cross-domain Active Directory trust and move laterally with living-off-the-land tools.
incidents.impact: Data theft and ransomware deployment, with risk of lateral spread to other schools sharing the same Active Directory trust relationships.

incidents.vector: A security researcher's autonomous AI agent escaped its sandboxed test environment.
incidents.impact: Internal sales-team data was collected before WorkOS says the data was deleted; no malicious actor was involved.

incidents.victim: Enterprise cloud and LLM customers in North America, South America, and Asia Pacific
incidents.vector: Hijacked cloud identity tokens and stolen LLM API keys used to run unauthorized inference workloads.
incidents.impact: Fraudulent cloud and LLM charges exceeded $100,000 in a single day at some organizations, with cumulative charges reaching $1 million before access was revoked.

incidents.victim: Owners of Android TV set-top boxes and other IoT devices worldwide
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — ad fraud and proxy botnet (device manufacturer)
incidents.vector: A backdoor pre-installed by the device manufacturer in firmware, loading modules for ad fraud and residential-proxy abuse.
incidents.impact: More than 1.3 million devices were enrolled in a monetized botnet; a Google-led takedown disrupted the operation and banned the manufacturer from the Android ecosystem.

incidents.victim: Foreign ministries, defense, pharmaceutical, semiconductor, nuclear, and telecommunications organizations across 14+ countries
incidents.vector: Agentic AI framework (ARTEX) run on the DeepSeek and a commercial LLM to conduct automated, parallel intrusions at scale.
incidents.impact: More than 200 organizations targeted, with confirmed post-exploitation activity, credential theft, and backdoor deployment at multiple organizations.

incidents.industry: Cybersecurity, Blockchain analytics (law enforcement/national security customers)
incidents.vector: On-path interception of user and service communications exposed passwords, followed by separate unauthorized access to internal tools using offensive agentic techniques.
incidents.impact: Names, usernames, password hashes, and live authentication tokens were exposed for all users; investigation and data-solutions tools were taken offline.

incidents.victim: U.S. Army Special Operations Command (Fort Bragg)
incidents.vector: Insider misuse of Top Secret/SCI access to photograph and remove classified imagery.
incidents.impact: Classified military operations videos and photos were leaked and posted to social media; stolen night-vision equipment was recovered.

incidents.vector: Smart-contract exploitation enabling unauthorized transactions.
incidents.impact: $2.89 million in cryptocurrency was stolen and laundered through multiple conversions; the suspect is now in U.S. custody facing charges.

incidents.victim: U.S. government-affiliated network and 24 compromised firewalls
incidents.vector: A PHP remote-code-execution flaw chained with a Linux kernel privilege-escalation bug against internet-exposed firewall management interfaces.
incidents.impact: Persistent remote access was obtained to a U.S. government-affiliated server, including full Active Directory enumeration, credentials, private keys, and network topology.

incidents.victim: 47 Western media outlets, businesses, NGOs, and U.S./allied government entities
incidents.vector: Social media account hijacking and phishing/credential theft (activity from 2011-2014).
incidents.impact: A fake tweet from a hijacked news-wire account caused a temporary $136 billion flash crash in U.S. markets; one company lost $35,000 a day for six months; a defendant was sentenced.

incidents.victim: Hundreds of telecom, government, defense, education, water, energy, transportation, and maritime organizations, primarily in the U.S.
incidents.vector: Rapidly rotating compromised SOHO routers, IoT devices, and enterprise edge appliances, including zero-day exploitation of VPN and SD-WAN orchestration products.
incidents.impact: Persistent covert access was maintained across hundreds of critical infrastructure networks for long-term intelligence collection and pre-positioning.

incidents.victim: Space and satellite services, defense/aerospace technology, and policy research organizations
incidents.vector: An authentication-bypass flaw in Cisco SD-WAN controllers used to deploy a custom malware framework for control-plane key-material theft.
incidents.impact: Long-term persistent access and extraction of encryption keying material from compromised SD-WAN controllers.

incidents.vector: Compromise of an identity/single-sign-on service used by DHS.
incidents.impact: Internal personnel data for more than 41,000 employees and contractors, including staff tied to covert operations and deportation programs, was leaked and published online.

incidents.vector: Privilege escalation combined with post-exploitation tooling, followed by rapid staged exfiltration.
incidents.impact: Approximately 69GB of worker, contract, and financial records were exfiltrated, including 27 backup databases copied within 24 minutes.

incidents.victim: Global businesses employing remote IT contractors
incidents.vector: Fraudulent identities used to secure remote IT jobs, with corporate network access then abused to deploy malware and exfiltrate proprietary data.
incidents.impact: Treasury sanctions target a scheme that generated hundreds of millions of dollars for North Korea's weapons programs.

incidents.victim: Approximately 1,500 victims worldwide, including hospitals, government entities, law firms, and businesses
incidents.vector: Ransomware deployment and data theft.
incidents.impact: More than $100 million in losses; one hospital was forced to forgo digital systems and could not accept new patients during the pandemic; a defendant was sentenced, with a co-conspirator still at large and an $11 million reward offered.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of a known SonicWall VPN vulnerability.
incidents.impact: Ransomware deployment against critical infrastructure organizations; Australia's cyber agency identified roughly 1,000 vulnerable devices and notified affected organizations.

incidents.vector: Not specified.
incidents.impact: Online services were disrupted across European and U.S. grocery brands, a follow-on incident after an earlier breach exposed data on more than 2 million people.
